title: Practice: Surface Area - Cones and Spheres

questions.stem: A cone has radius 5 cm and vertical height 12 cm. What is its total surface area in terms of pi?
questions.explanation: First find slant height: l = sqrt(5^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(25 + 144) = sqrt(169) = 13 cm. Total SA = pi r l + pi r^2 = pi(5)(13) + pi(25) = 65 pi + 25 pi = 90 pi cm squared.

questions.stem: What is the surface area of a sphere with radius 8 cm? Give your answer to the nearest cm squared.
questions.explanation: SA = 4 pi r^2 = 4 pi (64) = 256 pi = 804.247... which rounds to 804 cm squared.

questions.stem: A solid hemisphere has radius 7 cm. What is its total surface area in terms of pi?
questions.explanation: Total SA of hemisphere = curved surface + flat circle = 2 pi r^2 + pi r^2 = 3 pi r^2 = 3 pi (49) = 147 pi cm squared. A common error is to forget the flat circular face.

questions.stem: A cone has radius 6 cm and slant height 10 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of pi?
questions.explanation: Curved SA = pi r l = pi x 6 x 10 = 60 pi cm squared.

questions.stem: A sphere has a surface area of 324 pi cm squared. What is its radius?
questions.explanation: SA = 4 pi r^2 = 324 pi. So r^2 = 324/4 = 81, giving r = 9 cm.
